openai.feedback:
- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-test/scripts/lib/screenshot_viewport.py:51
- Finding: Invalid numeric viewport declarations can silently fall back to 1280x800. The regex only recognizes three or four digits, so `width=99` and `width=10000` are ignored instead of producing the per-screen error AC1 requires. It also partially accepts `width=390.5` as 390.
- Suggestion: Parse the complete width value, then validate its integer format and range. Return an error for invalid numeric declarations while retaining support for `width=device-width`.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-design/scripts/checks/record-non-ui-frs.py:69
- Finding: Any occurrence of “screen” anywhere in a capability section is treated as an unmapped screen reference, before checking `UI: none`. For example, `Requirement: Store screen capture events` followed by `UI: none` is returned in `ask[]`, although the section explicitly declares no UI and names no Mockup.
- Suggestion: Distinguish actual mockup or screen references from ordinary requirement prose. Honor an explicit `UI: none` unless the section also identifies a concrete conflicting mockup.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib/autonomous_override.py:206
- Finding: An invalid tolerance is recorded as a refusal reason but execution continues to `float(tolerance)`. With `tolerance: null` and otherwise valid attribution, the rule raises `TypeError` instead of returning `allowed: false` with reasons. The existing tolerance tests cover numeric values only.
- Suggestion: Return the refusal before recomputing evidence when tolerance validation fails, or guard recomputation behind valid prerequisites. Add a test for null and nonnumeric tolerance values.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The implementation covers the main workflows, but declaration parsing and refusal handling need these specific corrections.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
## Findings

- **Category: security / bug — Severity: high**
  `plugins/shipwright-test/scripts/lib/screenshot_check.py` (~line in `run_screenshot_check`, `vp = screenshot_viewport.screen_viewport(entry, _map_entry(mockup, smap), [p for p in (source, approved) if p])`)
  `source` is `_builder_file(root, mockup) or approved` — the **built app's file**, i.e. code the agent just wrote. It is passed first in the sources list, so a `<meta name="shipwright-viewport" content="390x800">` (or phone-frame markup) in the *implementation* picks the viewport a screen is compared at. This is exactly the hole the design closes ("test wiring cannot pick the size a red screen is compared at", step-3.7b: "It is 1280x800 unless the **approved package** declares another one"): the implementation can shrink the comparison to its own favor and turn a `fail` into a `pass`.
  Suggestion: derive the viewport only from the approved side — pass `[p for p in (approved,) if p]` (plus the screen-map entry); never consult the builder file.

- **Category: spec — Severity: medium**
  `plugins/shipwright-test/scripts/lib/screenshot_viewport.py` — `_PHONE_ROOT_RE`
  AC1 says "a `phone-frame`/`mobile-frame` element **in the markup**" declares a phone screen. The implementation only recognizes the element when it is the *first child of `<body>`* (`<body ...>\s*<el ... phone-frame`). A mockup with a wrapper (`<body><div class="app"><div class="phone-frame">…`) — the common shape — silently falls back to 1280x800, recreating the run-20 desktop-vs-phone false failure the feature exists to fix. The tests pin the strict behavior rather than the spec.
  Suggestion: match a phone-frame element anywhere in the body markup (comments/scripts already stripped), or at minimum also accept the frame as any early structural element, not only the first child.

- **Category: spec — Severity: medium**
  `plugins/shipwright-design/scripts/checks/record-non-ui-frs.py` — `non_ui_verdict`
  Two deviations from AC3 ("a capability whose `brief.md` section names no Mockup **(or states `UI: none`)**" is recorded):
  1. The `_SCREEN_REF_RE` screen-reference veto runs *before* the `UI: none` check and matches the bare words "screen"/"screens" anywhere in the section. A section stating `UI: none` and also mentioning "no screens are needed" is returned in `ask[]` instead of being recorded — the parameterized test even pins this as intended, but the spec says `UI: none` wins. (The Mockup-name veto for the *Source* line is right; the anywhere-word veto is not.)
  2. A section with **no `Source:` line at all** names no Mockup, so per the spec it should be recorded; the code returns it in `ask[]` ("says nothing about a screen").
  Suggestion: check `UI: none` first, restrict the contradiction veto to the `Source:` line naming a Mockup, and treat a Source-less section as non-UI (or explicitly amend the spec/docs if "ask" is intended).

- **Category: bug — Severity: medium**
  `plugins/shipwright-test/scripts/lib/screenshot_check.py` — `_map_entry`
  The screen-map entry for a mockup is found by using the mockup's `NN` prefix as a **1-based list index** into `screen-map["screens"]`. If the package's screen-map is not sorted exactly by the NN prefixes (a screen-map entry `viewport` is the whole point of this feature, and nothing in the package format guarantees ordering), the wrong entry's `viewport` is applied to the wrong screen — silently comparing a phone screen at a desktop size or vice versa. The comment says "same NN prefix rule as `_approved_for`", but `_approved_for` resolves a *file*, this resolves *metadata*; the fragility now has pixel-level consequences.
  Suggestion: match the screen-map entry by its mockup/screen id (as `apply-brief-package.py` does) rather than by positional index.

- **Category: spec — Severity: low**
  `plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib/autonomous_override.py` — `decide_screenshot_override`, the autonomy re-check
  `is_autonomous` accepts a run with `brief_package` set regardless of autonomy, but the second check requires `autonomy ∈ {guided, autonomous}`. A run with a brief package and no/other `autonomy` key — which the spec calls autonomous ("a brief package makes a run autonomous whatever its autonomy setting") — is refused. If the config schema guarantees `autonomy` defaults to `guided` this is dead-safe; if not, the rule silently degrades to a question for exactly the runs it exists for. Suggestion: default missing `autonomy` to `guided` explicitly, or drop the re-check for brief-package runs whose autonomy isn't `unattended`.

- **Category: test — Severity: low**
  `plugins/shipwright-test/tests/test_screenshot_viewport.py` — `test_the_capture_script_honours_a_jobs_viewport`
  This "test" only greps the `.mjs` source for the strings `"job.viewport"` and `"viewport: jobViewport"`. A rename, a wrong binding, or a broken viewport path in the node script would still pass; the actual consumer behavior (per-job viewport in `newContext`) is untested. Suggestion: assert on the parsed behavior (e.g. run the mjs against a stubbed browser or extract the jobViewport computation), or delete the string-grep so it doesn't create false confidence.

- **Category: test — Severity: low**
  `plugins/shipwright-build/tests/test_size_target_rule.py`
  Both tests are substring assertions over markdown prose; they cannot detect a rule that is stated but not followed (there is no executable spec-reviewer behavior to test here, so this is arguably the ceiling — but note the build SKILL sentence lands in the paragraph about mockup contradiction, where an agent skimming for "Design decision" may miss it). No action required beyond awareness; the size-target carve-out itself is only prose-enforced end to end.

Checked and found sound: the path-containment and shell-metacharacter handling in `autonomous_override.py` (safe-rel regex + `resolve()` + `is_relative_to`, validated-only reason text — the `pwned` test confirms), the committed-ADR check against `git show HEAD:`, the fail-closed module loading, the `phase_gate.override_hook` re-check consistency with `AUTONOMOUS_REASON_PREFIX`, and the idempotency of `record-non-ui-frs.py`'s second run.

## Overall

The autonomous-override rule is genuinely conservative and well-tested; the per-screen viewport work has one real security-shaped hole (the built file can choose its own comparison size) and two spec deviations (phone-frame detection too narrow, non-UI verdict too eager to ask). Ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
